NRL Late Mail: Round 26 - Cleary set to debut
Halfback Jett Cleary will make his debut alongside Luke Hanson after the Warriors chose to rest Te Maire Martin and Chanel Harris-Tavita.
Martin was named on Tuesday to return from a hamstring complaint which kept him out of the last three matches against Penrith, Brisbane and South Sydney.
However, he has been omitted as has Harris-Tavita who has a minor hamstring issue. Both will train fully next week to line up in the final regular season match against the Sea Eagles.
Roosters skipper James Tedesco will again look to make his comeback from an ankle injury after being named to face the Dolphins.
Tedesco suffered the injury in Round 22 against the Cowboys and has struggled to get it right across the past fortnight, twice being named to play before being a late withdrawal.

NRL Super Saturday has just two weeks remaining and fans will want to make the most of the exciting rugby league which is on offer. Titans vs Rabbitohs Predictions & Tips: NRL Round 26 2026
Only playing for one half
Leading 16-8 at HT against the Sharks in front of their home fans, things were looking positive for the Titans and hopes were high that they could replicate that effort in the second half. Unfortunately, positive execution eluded them as they suffered a 30-22 loss. Despite completing at 84% with 47% possession, they managed 8.7m per carry and made 499 PCM’s. Their defence was poor though, missing 39 tackles and conceding 9 line breaks. While this happens, they will continue to be outplayed by better teams high than them on the ladder.
Consistently inconsistent (again)
It was another inconsistent performance from the Rabbitohs at home in their 45-26 loss to the Warriors. Another slow start saw them trail 26-8 at HT before they fought their way back into the match. Behind 32-26 with 20 minutes remaining, the result slipped away as their execution again declined. With 49% possession, they completed at just 77%, ran for 8.3m per carry and made 9 line breaks. There is no doubt that they can compete with the contending teams, but it is their ability to maintain this intensity which is continually letting them down over 80 minutes.
Stats that matter
- The Rabbitohs have won the past 10 games against the Titans, taking their record at this ground to 93%. The Titans win just 43% of games at home.
- In the past 5 games between these two sides, only one has been decided by fewer than 14 points. This has the average sitting at 19.6 points. They’re usually high scoring contests too; the average total is 51.6 points.
- The Rabbitohs are the superior team on both sides of the ball this season. They score 27ppg in attack compared to the Titans 19ppg. Defensively, things are closer, with the Rabbitohs allowing 24ppg just ahead of the Titans 27ppg.
Motivated by the Finals
It is a simple equation for the Rabbitohs in this contest: win, and your spot in the Finals is cemented in. This will carry huge ramifications as it releases the pressure that a rivalry next round will bring. Removing this emotion will serve their squad well as they push towards the Finals. The possibility that both Humphries and Mitchell will return is a huge boost for the visitors. The short turnaround into this game for the Titans will impact their fatigue levels. They faded away in the second half last week and are guilty of this throughout 2026. With their talent proven at different times, they can cause an upset but a lot would have to go right for that to occur. If the Rabbitohs are a serious contender or wish to be considered as that, this is a game that they must dominate and remove all doubt over the potential winner. Their edges can build on the strong platform set in the middle and, provided the ruck speed is to their liking, they can dictate the terms of the match. Their positive record against the Titans speaks for itself and they should build on that again with a win here.

'A beautiful scene': Walker ready for Arrow's special milestone
Jai Arrow will make a special return to the field at Cbus Super Stadium against the Titans on Saturday, with team-mates excited to see him suit up in South Sydney colours again.
The NRL has approved a unique rule change allowing Arrow to take part in the final two games of the season for the Rabbitohs and reach the 100-game milestone that was cruelly interrupted by his diagnosis of motor neurone disease.
Related Rabbitohs
Jai Arrow receives NRL support to achieve special milestone
Arrow will lead out the Rabbitohs for the opening seconds before being interchanged and spending the remainder of the match on the bench alongside his team mates.
For best mate Cody Walker, seeing Arrow decked out in the red and green again will be a moment packed with plenty of emotion.
“To be able to get out there, where he grew up, his old club, it will be a beautiful scene, but an emotional one for those involved,” Walker said.
Arrow spent three seasons with the Titans before joining South Sydney in 2021, where he and Walker quickly formed one of the club's most infectious friendships.
Jai Arrow gets birthday surprise from The Wiggles and the PM
Five years later, that bond has remained unchanged.
“He’s a big part of our club, a big part of our team and he’s a big part of my life since he came to the club.”
And while Arrow’s playing days may have come to an end, Walker said his energy around the club remained the same.
“He’s still one of the loudest in the squad when he’s around training,” Walker said.
“The banter is still flying around the group like no tomorrow. You can see that he’s beaming inside and it means a hell of a lot to him.”
Related Match Preview
Titans v Rabbitohs: Fifita sidelined; Trell on track
The 31-year-old was just two games short of 100 when his diagnosis forced him to retire, leaving the former Queensland Origin forward without the chance to reach the club milestone that once seemed inevitable.
Now, he will get that chance - a moment that will be about far more than just a number.
“Everyone in the rugby league community has done a beautiful job at supporting Jai in different ways. He’ll be feeling the love," Walker said.
“That’s one of the beauties of our great game, that when one of our own is going through a bit, we all band together regardless of what team everyone plays for.”
Related Titans
Titans reveal Stand with Jai jersey for Bunnies clash
And the special moment would not have been possible without the people behind the scenes, including Rabbitohs coach Wayne Bennett, who helped push for the unprecedented rule change with the NRL.
“A lot of the guys in the background have to be commended and congratulated on getting this over the line,” Walker said.
“I think Wayne was one of those guys who took it to Peter and the guys at the NRL.”

items.snippet: ‘A big thing’: Bennett reveals how ‘special’ Arrow plan was hatched    Nine.com.au
items.body_excerpt:
Rabbitohs coach Wayne Bennett has explained how Jai Arrow ’s 99th and 100th games will happen, while paying tribute to the outpouring of support from the wider NRL community after the star’s diagnosis with motor neurone disease.
Arrow was forced to retire effective immediately earlier this season after revealing the MND diagnosis , which saw him finish on 98 games for South Sydney.
Jai Arrow will take the field on Saturday. Getty Images
The tough forward has been the heart and soul of Souths since arriving at the club in 2021, becoming one of the Bunnies’ most beloved players.
With a potential milestone in the red and green jersey ripped away from Arrow due to his retirement, Bennett and the club found a way to make it happen.
In the final two rounds, Arrow will run out alongside his teammates and will be on the field when the referee blows the whistle for kick off .
The 31-year-old will then leave the field and be replaced by Cameron Murray .
Speaking to media on Friday morning, Bennett explained why he pushed for the incredible gesture and why it was so important for Arrow.
Read more
Luai already cashing in on PNG deal as new sponsor deal unveiled
“This is what it means to players, to be a 100-game player at a club is a big thing, it’s sometimes even bigger than 200 or 300,” the coach said.
“He was on 98 and thinking about it all, knowing what it would mean to him, he’s been a wonderful warrior and a guy made to play 100 games at a club. We wanted it to be authentic, we didn’t want it to just be ‘we’ll give you this’.
“We knew he couldn’t fulfil all the commitments of playing 80 minutes and all the other stuff, but through a bit of a process, we got to a place where we’re at now.
“When the referee blows the whistle in the NRL, that’s the start of the game. If you’re on the field at that time and you do your hamstring – that would still count as a game. They will blow the whistle and then he will leave the field.
“His replacement will come on and that’s not an interchange replacement, the league have been kind enough to make sure that didn’t happen.”
Bennett said the way NRL officials and fans from all clubs have rallied around Arrow in recent months proves how special the game can be.
“I wouldn’t like to take all the credit for it, he’s our player and that’s not something we’ve walked away from or will ever walk away from,” Bennett said.
“Rugby league people have been wonderful in how they’ve handled it and the support they’ve given us and him. That’s what makes the game so special to me.
“I’ve been in a lot of instances in the game with major injuries and stuff like that with players, and the fans have always reached out ... we’re very fortunate.”
Souths will face the Titans – one of Arrow’s former teams – on Saturday afternoon, before a round 27 showdown with arch rivals the Sydney Roosters.

‘He will’: Wayne Bennett confirms Latrell Mitchell will play in a huge boost for the Bunnies ahead of the finals
The return of one of rugby league’s biggest stars could turn the premiership race on its head, with the top-four teams now having to worry about a major Sydney club.
Three simple words from South Sydney coach Wayne Bennett have confirmed what all NRL fans wanted to know with superstar centre Latrell Mitchell set to make his long-awaited return from injury in a pre-finals Bunnies boost.
Mitchell hasn’t played since the round 11 loss to the Dolphins on May 15, with the rep star battling a nerve problem in his back that led to an issue in his calf.
The 29-year-old was in the form of his life with 11 tries in just nine appearances, including four in one freakish performance against the Dragons.
The Rabbitohs have been up and down with him on the sidelines, but they loom as a genuine premiership threat with Mitchell, Cam Murray and Cody Walker all on the field.
Latrell Mitchell has been cleared to play against the Titans on Saturday afternoon. Picture: Thomas Lisson
Mitchell missed the entire State of Origin campaign for the Blues and there were genuine fears that he would miss the rest of the season.
But after he was a late scratching last week, Mitchell has been given the all clear to take on the Titans on Saturday afternoon where he’ll come off the bench and will likely play left centre.
Others you may like
“Yes he will,” Bennett declared when asked if his strike weapon would play.
“The boys have been great without him, so we just need to get him back playing now and not put him under any unnecessary pressure where he thinks that he’s got to do something special for us because we can handle ourselves pretty well.
“It’s great to have him back and get a bit of condition and contact behind him.”
Bennett was asked if Mitchell’s return was papering over the injury cracks and if he would need more medical attention at the end of the year.
But his response suggested the powerhouse centre was fully fit.
“He’s totally cleared to play,” Bennett said.
Tallis Duncan will move to the back row when Latrell Mitchell comes on.
“There are no needles involved, there are no painkillers involved, there’s nothing. He’s 100 per cent fit.”
Mitchell’s return is a timely boost for the Rabbitohs who will realistically seal a spot in the finals with a win this weekend given how strong their for and against is compared with the Bulldogs who are two points behind them with two rounds to go.
Bennett has a plan for how he wants to use Mitchell who will most likely come on at left centre, shifting Tallis Duncan to the back row.
More Coverage
His goalkicking will be integral for a team that has struggled from the tee in recent weeks, with teammates just happy to get their great mate back so close to the finals.
“He brings himself, you know? His X-factor,” Duncan said.
“He’s Latrell, so any time you can be on the same field as someone like that, you know he’s a big moments player. When we need a moment, he’ll come up with the footy.”

items.body_excerpt:
Rimoni ready to rumble as Titans aim to build on team record
Teenage Titan Fanua Rimoni may think she has “no reputation” behind her, but expect that all to change if she keeps on putting in performances like the one she produced against Brisbane.
Having just turned 19 last month, the powerful prop topped the run metres for the game with 189 from 16 carries, with 82 of them being post-contact as the Gold Coast claimed a 28-20 derby win.
Starting out primarily playing rugby union while in New Zealand, Rimoni found a love for league playing with Wellington Orcas and at various Māori rugby league tournaments before moving to Brisbane to play with the Norths Devils Under 19 side last year.
Fanua Rimoni made her NRLW debut against the Bulldogs in Round 2. ©NRL Images
Progressing to the BMD Premiership later in the 2025, it has been a rapid rise for Rimoni who was promoted from a development deal to the top 24 earlier this year, becoming one of six players to debut with the Titans this year.
Since making an unexpected debut in Round 2, the Wellington-born talent hasn’t looked out of place in the top grade, despite stepping into the boots left by injured Jillaroos forward Jess Elliston, who suffered a season-ending MCL injury in Round 1.
“I definitely didn't expect (to debut in the NRLW this year), especially that early in the season, and to be starting as well, was a shock to me,” Rimoni said.
“But the girls have been so welcoming and Jess, I just pick her brain as much as I can and she's so helpful and so welcoming for me as well.
“I really enjoy (playing NRLW), I think especially being at this club, I think the culture's so good, a lot of the girls talk about it, but I think it's real.
“The culture is so strong and the girls make it easier, the coaches make it easier for me to transition into a starting forward in this space.”
Related Match Preview
Titans v Raiders: Chapman sidelined; Dodd promoted to start
Now firmly established in the starting pack, Rimoni has played her part in helping the team achieve a club record seven NRLW wins in a row, but wasn’t getting too far ahead of herself knowing the challenge ahead against the Raiders.
Like the Titans, Canberra are a team on the up and looking to lock in a maiden finals berth, with a forward pack featuring revered workhorse Simaima Taufa, Queensland prop Sophie Holyman and England representative Hollie-Mae Dodd.
“I think just having this little bit of history with us is lifting us a lot more, I think,” Rimoni said of the task ahead.
“We're not getting complacent every week, which is good, and every week we're just getting hungrier and wanting to get it even more.
Related Titans
Coasting along: Local Levi loving new role in rugby league
“I think I'm just more so just still trying to find my feet.
“Obviously (I look up to) Georgia Hale, Jess Elliston, they the big names in the NRLW, especially the middles, I look up to them and look up to their leadership and obviously their playing style.
“For me, I've got really no reputation behind me, so I like being the underdog and trying to just put my best foot forward for the team, for the girls.
“I don't really mind who we're facing, I think we go hard every week.”
